long_femur.guidance: A longer femur relative to the torso pushes the hips further back to keep the bar over the mid-foot. This necessitates a more horizontal back angle. Consider a low-bar placement to center the mass better over the hips, or use a wider stance and weightlifting shoes with an elevated heel to allow the knees to travel further forward and keep the torso more upright.

short_torso.guidance: A proportionally short torso requires the back angle to be more horizontal to maintain balance over the mid-foot. Focus heavily on core stability and lower back strength. Low-bar squats often feel more natural.

long_torso.guidance: A long torso relative to the femurs allows for a very upright squatting position. High bar or front squats will feel very natural and allow for deep ranges of motion with less lower back strain.

long_arms.guidance: Long arms (or a large arm span relative to height) are highly advantageous for deadlifting. They reduce the total range of motion and allow for a more upright starting back angle, reducing sheer force on the lumbar spine.

short_arms.guidance: Short arms require a deeper starting hip position and a more horizontal back angle to reach the bar. If conventional deadlifts cause excessive lower back rounding or discomfort, consider transitioning to a sumo deadlift which artificially 'lengthens' the arms relative to the stance.

long_arms.guidance: Long arms significantly increase the range of motion in the bench press and can place greater stress on the shoulders at the bottom of the movement. Utilizing a wider grip (within legal competition limits) can help reduce the ROM, or incorporating a slight arch to elevate the chest.

short_arms.guidance: Short arms are advantageous for the bench press as they naturally restrict the range of motion and typically allow for heavier weights to be lifted safely. A standard or even slightly narrower grip can be highly effective.

long_arms.guidance: Long arms require a longer bar path to lockout. Focus on maintaining strict core and glute stability throughout the extended time under tension.
